edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.XVIII (the day of victory; Hilarianus)

source_text: Inluxit dies uictoriae illorum, et processerunt de carcere in amphitheatrum, quasi in caelum, hilares et uultu decori; si forte gaudio pauentes non timore. Sequebatur Perpetua placido incessu, ut matrona Christi, ut dei delicata, uigore oculorum deiciens omnium conspectum. Item Felicitas, saluam se peperisse gaudens ut ad bestias pugnaret, a sanguine ad sanguinem, ab obstetrice ad retiarium, lotura post partum baptismo secundo. Et cum deducti essent in portam et cogerentur habitum induere, uiri quidem sacerdotum Saturni, feminae uero sacratarum Cereri, generosa illa in finem usque constantia repugnauit. Dicebat enim: Ideo ad hoc sponte peruenimus, ne libertas nostra obduceretur; ideo animam nostram addiximus, ne tale aliquid faceremus; hoc uobiscum pacti sumus. Agnouit iniustitia iustitiam: concessit tribunus, quomodo erant, simpliciter inducerentur. Perpetua psallebat, caput iam Aegyptii calcans; Reuocatus et Saturninus et Saturus populo spectanti comminabantur. Dehinc ut sub conspectu Hilariani peruenerint, gestu et nutu coeperunt Hilariano dicere: Tu nos, inquiunt, te autem deus. Ad hoc populus exasperatus flagellis eos uexari per ordinem uenatorum postulauit; et utique illi gratulati sunt quod aliquid et de dominicis passionibus essent consecuti.
pass_a_gloss: The day of their victory shone forth, and they went out from the prison into the amphitheater as into heaven, glad and comely in face, if trembling, trembling from joy not fear. Perpetua was following with tranquil gait, as Christ's matron, as God's delicate one, throwing down everyone's stare with strength of eyes. Also Felicitas, glad because she had borne safely so that she might fight against beasts, from blood to blood, from midwife to net-man, about to wash after birth with a second baptism. And when they had been brought down into the gate and were forced to put on clothing, the men indeed that of Saturn's priests, the women indeed that of Ceres' devotees, that high-born woman struggled against to the end with persistence. For she was saying: For this reason we arrived here willingly, lest our freedom be covered over; for this reason we handed over our soul, lest we do anything of that sort; this we bargained with you. Injustice acknowledged justice: the tribune allowed that they be led in simply as they were. Perpetua was psalm-singing, now trampling the Egyptian's head; Revocatus and Saturninus and Saturus were threatening the looking people. Next when they came under Hilarianus's sight, with gesture and nod they began to say to Hilarianus: You us, they say, but God you. Toward this the embittered people demanded that they be harassed with whips through the row of hunters; and they indeed congratulated themselves because they had also attained something of the Lord's sufferings.
pass_b_english: The day of their victory dawned, and they processed from the prison into the amphitheater as if into heaven, cheerful and radiant of face, trembling if at all with joy rather than fear. Perpetua followed with calm step, as a matron of Christ, as God's cherished one, casting down the gaze of all by the vigor of her eyes. Felicitas came on too, rejoicing that she had delivered safely so that she could fight the beasts, going from blood to blood, from midwife to net-fighter, to wash after her childbirth in a second baptism.

And when they had been led to the gate and were compelled to put on the dress, the men that of the priests of Saturn and the women that of the votaries of Ceres, that noble woman resisted with steadfastness to the very end. For she kept saying: We came to this of our own accord precisely so that our freedom would not be veiled; for this reason we pledged our life, so that we would do no such thing; this is what we agreed with you. Injustice recognized justice: the tribune conceded that they be brought in simply as they were. Perpetua was singing psalms, already trampling the Egyptian's head underfoot; Revocatus and Saturninus and Saturus kept threatening the watching crowd. Then when they came into Hilarianus's view, they began to say to Hilarianus by gesture and nod: You condemn us, they say, but God will condemn you. At this the enraged people demanded that they be scourged in file past the hunters; and they indeed rejoiced that they had obtained some share in the Lord's sufferings.

choices.term: ut matrona Christi, ut dei delicata
choices.english: as a matron of Christ, as God's cherished one
choices.why: double ut with nominative nouns describes the manner of her placido incessu, matrona keeps Roman social status and delicata means favored dependent, not wife

choices.english: to wash after her childbirth in a second baptism
choices.why: future participle lotura expresses purpose and ablative baptismo secundo means by martyrdom understood as baptism of blood after literal birth-blood
rejected: about to bathe after delivery in a second baptism ceremony

choices.english: lest our freedom be covered over
choices.why: passive subjunctive of obduco after ne is a purpose clause, libertas is their free status as voluntary martyrs threatened by forced cult dress
